notes: Event date: 9 March 1945 (CMH ETO-OB chronology for the 65th Infantry Division: entered combat 9 March 1945; arrived on the Continent 26 January 1945). Event definition: the CMH page dates the division's entry into combat; the table lists XX Corps and Third Army from 1 March. Relationship: XX Corps unspecified_subordination (from 1 Mar 45, CMH table); Third Army assigned (from 1 Mar 45, CMH table); 12th Army Group assigned (from 18 Jan 45, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: Boulay-Moselle (CMH ETO-OB command-post list, R524 p. 200: listed 7 March 1945; 2 days before the row); the town centre stands for the command post. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Boulay-Moselle. Event support: moderate (CMH page only; no Green Book narrative read for this entry). Location support: moderate (nearest earlier command post, 2 days before the row; the position on the date is not documented). Review (spot check, 26 October 2026): the date of the division's entry into combat is disputed between two CMH products and nothing is changed: old 9 March 1945 (the ETO-OB page, kept), new unchanged; the CMH Combat Chronicle of the 65th Infantry Division (Army Almanac 1950, history.army.mil) says first elements entered the line on 5 March 1945 and the division as a whole took over the Saar sector from Orscholz to Wadgassen on 8 March 1945, with the first attack on 17 March; Wikipedia repeats the chronicle. The row therefore stands on the ETO-OB page alone for its date, and the confidence stays 0.5; the question of which date marks the entry is open for Scott.
